changelog: fix: the read-direction token (_R1/_R2) was matched anywhere in a FASTQ filename instead of only at the end, so any sample whose own name contained R1/R2 was mis-parsed. 'Bacteria_R1_1.fq.gz' resolved to sample 'Bacteria', splitting one library into two unpaired halves and letting two different samples share a name; worse, the manual-pairing mate guess rewrote it to 'Bacteria_R2_2.fq.gz', pairing one sample's forward reads with a DIFFERENT sample's reverse reads — which does not fail loudly, it produces a plausible ASV table. The token is now anchored before the extension (_R1 / _1 / _R1_001), with the old loose rule kept only as a verified fallback for trimmer output such as Sample_R1_val_1.fq.gz. The pipeline now also refuses to start when R1 and R2 files do not line up or two samples resolve to the same name, and the upload screen warns about both before the run. Second fix: filterAndTrim writes no output file for a sample whose reads all fail, and derepFastq() then aborted the entire job with 'Not all provided files exist.' — after the error model had already been learned. Zero-read samples are now dropped with a named warning and the run continues with the rest. Also: push_github.sh always reported 'Cancelled' no matter what you typed at the confirmation prompt — its `ssh -T git@github.com` preflight inherited the terminal as stdin and swallowed it, so the later `read` got EOF. ssh now runs with -n and the prompt reads from /dev/tty.

previous.2.8.2: fix: the PDF report kept reporting weasyprint as missing after it had been installed. The backend runs from its own venv (start.sh launches $APP_DIR/venv/bin/uvicorn), so a pip install typed at a cond
previous.2.8.1: add: single-run result report with QC, figures, a top-N ASV table and diversity; the merge-ceiling verdict now weighs read mass at the edge rather than using a fixed tolerance.
previous.2.8.0: add: PDF reports — report_builder.py, POST /report, and a 'PDF Report' button on each completed job.
previous.2.7.9: perf: species assignment runs in its own R process.
